newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks close stronger on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close stronger on technical rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed stronger on Friday as a technical rebound pushed up the blue chip Hang Seng Index by 386.06 points, or 2.60 percent, to 15,225.29. "This is a technical rebound since the market has been oversold on the daily chart," said Calvin Chan, technical analyst at J&A securities.
The market was volatile this week but brokers said buyers regained confidence after the index found support near 14,600.
"It's a very good rebound, I think, and surprising a lot of people," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
Blue chips were broadly higher with China Light rising HK$1.70 to HK$42.80 and Hongkong Telecom adding HK$0.70 to HK$18.15.
Property counters rose across the board on rotational buying. Sun Hung Kai Properties added HK$2.75 to HK$92.50 and New World Development gained HK$1.80 to HK$48.10.
Red chips outperformed Hang Seng constituent stocks, with the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index closing 134.43 points, or 4.22 percent, higher at 3,319.45.
Overall market turnover was HK$18.55 billion, up from HK$14.76 billion on Thursday.
Brokers said asset injection news and hopes of more acquisitions by red chips encouraged buying.

"China's guidelines or measures on red chips will end up with higher transparency in the stocks and this will lift investor confidence in China-affiliated stocks," said Hugo So, an analyst at Yamaichi.
China Everbright International jumped HK$0.65 to HK$4.90 after news it was in talks to buy a 25 percent stake in Hong Kong Shanghai Development Co Ltd.

Brokers also said news that Liu Chong Hing Bank was in talks with the COSCO Group and other parties about a possible capital injection fanned hopes that smaller banks might become targets of other mainland companies.
Wing Hang Bank surged HK$3.30 to HK$42.50 and Kwong On Bank soared HK$1.05 to HK$13.45. Blue chip Hang Seng Bank rose HK$4.50 to HK$111.50 and HSBC Holdings added HK$4.00 to HK$245.00.
July index futures ended 445 points higher at 15,335, a 110-point premium to the cash market. A total of 23,000 contracts changed hands.
